narrative: Material PL1__MAA1B42C shows regular but highly variable demand (CV=0.86) with a mean of 400 units/day across 209 working days. Lead times average 2.35 days with moderate variability (CV=0.39), exhibiting a bimodal pattern suggesting two supplier fulfillment modes. The combined lead-time demand sigma of 677 units requires a safety stock of 1,113 units for 95% service — nearly double the current SAP setting of 566. Storage capacity caps the order quantity at 3,259 units, yielding a 90% cost reduction vs the current policy by reducing annual orders from 368 to 31.
warnings: Storage capacity constraint is binding: EOQ 9962 capped to 3259 units (max_storage_units=4372, safety_stock=1113)
Current SAP safety stock (566) is below statistically derived optimum (1113); service level risk under current policy
Bimodal lead time distribution detected: two fulfillment modes (~1.8d and ~3.9d); supplier SLA review recommended

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is regular (non-zero fraction 87%) and approximately continuous, making a continuous-review (r,Q) policy appropriate. The fixed order quantity is set to the storage-capped EOQ which minimises total ordering and holding costs. A periodic-review policy would require a larger order-up-to level, worsening the capacity constraint.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage cap reduces order quantity from unconstrained EOQ of 9,962 to 3,259 units. This increases annual ordering cost from ~$750 to ~$2,317 vs unconstrained optimum, but total cost remains far below current policy. If demand grows or safety stock increases, the cap will tighten further — storage expansion would unlock additional savings of ~$1,500/year.
